summary:
I've been building tools for my own homelab that end up teaching more than any client project would — the constraints are real, there's just no one to hide them from.

The biggest one is a character-creation extension for SillyTavern. Before writing a line of it I ran a competitive survey of the existing extensions: one incumbent has 157 stars and does one-shot field generation plus a chat-to-refine loop, but nothing in the space does an interview first — asking questions before any field exists — or handles persona work at all. That's the gap I'm building into. Along the way I hit a genuinely obscure bug: a sentinel value in the picker code uses a literal null byte so it can never collide with a real filename, which means plain `grep` silently treats the whole file as binary and returns nothing — looks exactly like "this code doesn't exist" until you know to reach for `grep -a`.

A smaller, weirder one: I patch character lorebooks so a local model's prefix cache doesn't get busted every turn (keyword-triggered lore reshuffles the prompt each turn, which forces a full re-prefill — expensive on older GPU hardware). I fixed it upstream and thought I was done, until I found SillyTavern rewrites the character card back into memory on the first message of a new chat, silently reverting my patch. The fix had to survive a live in-memory write-back, not just a file edit.

I've also been building a Japanese-learning dashboard for myself, coached by an LLM. The interesting failure there wasn't technical, it was UX: my first placement test made me type romaji for kana I hadn't fully learned yet, and I stalled out three questions in. Swapping it for four-tile multiple choice with audio on each option, so it tests recognition instead of production, is the version I actually finish sessions on. It's a good reminder that a technically-working feature can still be testing the wrong skill.

highlights.oneLiner: Building an interview-first SillyTavern character-creation extension; surveyed the competitive field first
Patching character lorebooks so keyword-triggered lore stops busting the P100 prefix cache
Building a Japanese-learning dashboard coached by an LLM, tuning placement tests for recognition over typed production
